title: Spherical Harm
comment: Spherical Harm — Spherical harmonics is an orthogonal basis of eigenvectors of the Laplacian on the sphere. Eigenspaces of fixed frequency are rotation invariant. The basic tool to perform linear and invariant signal processing on the sphere. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_harmonics
alt_text: Spherical Harm. Spherical harmonics is an orthogonal basis of eigenvectors of the Laplacian on the sphere. Eigenspaces of fixed frequency are rotation invariant. The basic tool to perform linear and invariant signal processing on the sphere.

comment: Kmeans Plusplus — Classic reference: David Arthur and Sergei Vassilvitski, k-means++: the advantages of careful seeding, 2007. Defines an initialization of K-means which is log(K) optimal. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-means%2B%2B

title: Fokker Planck
comment: Fokker Planck — The three ways to solve Fokker-Planck equations: PDE evolution, stochastic (independent) or deterministic (coupled) particle systems. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fokker%E2%80%93Planck_equation
alt_text: Fokker Planck. The three ways to solve Fokker-Planck equations: PDE evolution, stochastic (independent) or deterministic (coupled) particle systems.

title: Shapley Folkman Starr
comment: Shapley Folkman Starr — Classic reference: R. M. Starr, Quasi-equilibria in markets with non-convex preferences, 1969. The Shapley-Folkman-Starr theorem state that the Minkowski sum "convexifies" sets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapley%E2%80%93Folkman_lemma

title: Central Limit Convol
comment: Central Limit Convol — The central limit theorem equivalently reads as the convergence of iterated convolutions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_limit_theorem

title: Steerable Pyramid
comment: Steerable Pyramid — Classic reference: E P Simoncelli, W T Freeman, E H Adelson and D J Heeger. Shiftable Multi-Scale Transforms, 1992. The steerable transform is the first efficient wavelet transform using oriented rotated filters. http://www.cns.nyu.edu/~eero/steerpyr/
alt_text: Steerable Pyramid. Classic reference: E P Simoncelli, W T Freeman, E H Adelson and D J Heeger. Shiftable Multi-Scale Transforms, 1992. The steerable transform is the first efficient wavelet transform using oriented rotated filters.

title: Fourier 2D
comment: Fourier 2D — 2-D Fourier vectors are tensor product of 1-D Fourier vectors. The product of a vertical and of a horizontal wave creates a diagonal wave! This is the secret of why orthogonal Fourier is so neat also in 2-D. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Fourier_transform#Multidimensional_DFT
alt_text: Fourier 2D. 2-D Fourier vectors are tensor product of 1-D Fourier vectors. The product of a vertical and of a horizontal wave creates a diagonal wave! This is the secret of why orthogonal Fourier is so neat also in 2-D.

title: Graphon
comment: Graphon — Classic reference: L. Lovasz and B. Szegedy. Limits of dense graph sequences, 2006. Graphons are both the continuous limit of dense discrete graphs and models to sample random dense graphs. The natural topology is the cut-metric. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphon
alt_text: Graphon. Classic reference: L. Lovasz and B. Szegedy. Limits of dense graph sequences, 2006. Graphons are both the continuous limit of dense discrete graphs and models to sample random dense graphs. The natural topology is the cut-metric.

title: Fourier Curve
comment: Fourier Curve — Fourier approximation of closed curves. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_series
alt_text: Fourier Curve. Fourier approximation of closed curves.

title: Min Degree Order
comment: Min Degree Order — Classic reference: H. M. Markowitz, The elimination form of the inverse and its application to linear programming, 1957. Introduces the minimum degree algorithm to perform sparse Cholesky factorizations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_degree_algorithm
alt_text: Min Degree Order. Classic reference: H. M. Markowitz, The elimination form of the inverse and its application to linear programming, 1957. Introduces the minimum degree algorithm to perform sparse Cholesky factorizations.

title: Color Quantize Approx
comment: Color Quantize Approx — Color 3D quantization versus approximation are two ways to reduce the information content of a color image. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_quantization
alt_text: Color Quantize Approx. Color 3D quantization versus approximation are two ways to reduce the information content of a color image.

title: Birkhoff Contrac
comment: Birkhoff Contrac — Classic reference: Garrett Birkhoff, Extensions of Jentzsch's theorem, 1957. Birkhoff's contraction for Hilbert's metric is a key tool to quantify convergence of Markov-Chains (Perron-Frobenius). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert_metric
alt_text: Birkhoff Contrac. Classic reference: Garrett Birkhoff, Extensions of Jentzsch's theorem, 1957. Birkhoff's contraction for Hilbert's metric is a key tool to quantify convergence of Markov-Chains (Perron-Frobenius).

title: Jko Flows
comment: Jko Flows — The heat equation is both the L2 gradient flow of Dirichlet energy and the Wasserstein flow of the entropy [Jordan, Kinderlehrer, Otto 1998]. This extends to non-linear diffusion. http://www-dimat.unipv.it/savare/Ravello2010/JKO.pdf

title: Ista
comment: Ista — Classic reference: M. Figueiredo, R. Nowak, An EM algorithm for wavelet-based image restoration, 2003. The first appearance of the celebrated Iterative Soft Thresholding Algorithm to solve the lasso. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasso_(statistics

title: Mac Adam Ellipses
comment: Mac Adam Ellipses — Color perception can be modeled using a Riemannian manifold. The Riemannian metric are called MacAdam ellipses. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacAdam_ellipse

title: Wigner Ville
comment: Wigner Ville — Classic reference: J. Ville, Theorie et Applications de la Notion de Signal Analytique, 1948. Introduces the Wigner-Ville distribution which mimics a probability distribution on the space-frequency plane. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigner_distribution_function

title: Dtw
comment: Dtw — Dynamic Time Warping aligns two time series by an increasing map. Solved in quadratic time by dynamic programming. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_time_warping
